title: Template engine: section uses value from outer context
statement:
# Template engine (`src/template.mjs`)

Minimalist "mustache"-style template engine. Users report that, on the orders screen, the template
`{{#pedido}}Pedido {{id}}{{#cupom}} (cupom {{codigo}}){{/cupom}}{{/pedido}}` displays the global promotional coupon
(`view.cupom`) on orders whose `cupom` field is `null`. The module must fully obey the contract below.

## API

- `render(template, view, partials = {})` → string. Equivalent to `compile(template)(view, partials)`.
- `compile(template)` → function `(view, partials = {}) => string`, reusable. Syntax errors are thrown already in `compile`.
- `parse(template)` → internal tree (free format); throws the same syntax errors.
- `escapeHtml(value)` → `String(value)` with **exactly** these six characters replaced, in a single pass (the produced text is not re-escaped): `&`→`&`, `<`→`<`, `>`→`>`, `"`→`"`, `'`→`'`, `` ` ``→```. E.g.: `escapeHtml('&')` → `'&amp;'`.
- `TemplateError` (subclass of `Error`, `name === 'TemplateError'`) with the property `pos` (0-based index in the template) and a message containing `posição <pos>`.
- `template` that is not a string → `TypeError`.
- Rendering never changes `view` (views frozen with `Object.freeze` work).

## Tags

A tag starts at `{{` and ends at the first following `}}`; if it starts with `{{{`, it ends at the first `}}}`. The sigil must come **immediately** after `{{`; the name is trimmed (surrounding spaces are ignored), so `{{ name }}` is the variable `name` and `{{ #a}}` is the **variable** named `#a`.

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `{{name}}` | variable, with `escapeHtml` |
| `{{{name}}}` or `{{& name}}` | variable without escaping |
| `{{#name}}…{{/name}}` | section |
| `{{^name}}…{{/name}}` | inverted section |
| `{{! any text }}` | comment (generates nothing) |
| `{{> name}}` | partial |

## Name resolution

During rendering there is a stack of contexts; the base is `view`. Each section that renders pushes a context (see below).

- `.` is the value of the top context.
- `@index` is the (0-based) index of the element in the **innermost** array iteration in progress (even if there are object sections pushed on top of it); outside iterations it is `undefined`.
- Dotted name `a.b.c`: the **first** segment (`a`) is looked up from the top to the base of the stack. Contexts that are not objects (or functions) — strings, numbers, booleans, `null` — are skipped. The search stops at the **first** context that **has the property** `a` — own or inherited through the prototype chain — **even if its value is `null` or `undefined`**; in that case the result is that value and outer contexts are not consulted. If no context has `a`, the value is `undefined`.
- The following segments (`b`, `c`) are read only from the value found, as properties (`value[seg]`), with no new search in the stack; if an intermediate value is `null`/`undefined`, the result is `undefined`. E.g.: `{{s.length}}` with `s: 'abc'` → `3`.

## Rendering

- Variables: `null`/`undefined` → `''`; other values → `String(value)` (with escaping, except in the unescaped forms). E.g.: `0` → `'0'`, `false` → `'false'`, `[1,2]` → `'1,2'`.
- A value is **empty** if it is falsy (`false`, `0`, `''`, `null`, `undefined`, `NaN`) or an array of length 0. Objects (including `{}`) are not empty.
- Section: empty value → renders nothing. Non-empty array → renders the content once per element, pushing the element (with its index for `@index`). Other value → renders once, pushing the value.
- Inverted section: renders the content once (without pushing anything) if and only if the value is empty.
- Partial `{{> name}}`: if `partials` has the **own** property `name` with a string value, that template is rendered in place with the current context stack; otherwise it generates nothing. Nested partials with depth above 50 (e.g.: infinite recursion) → `RangeError`.

## Standalone lines

A line ends at `\n` (a line ending in `\r\n` has the `\r` as part of the line break) or at the end of the template. If a **section, inverted section, closing or comment** tag is the only tag on its line and the rest of the line is only spaces/tabs, the whole line is removed from the output — including the spaces before the tag and the line break (`\n` or `\r\n`), if any. Variables (escaped or not) and partials never make a line standalone.

## Syntax errors (`TemplateError`)

- `{{` without `}}` (or `{{{` without `}}}`): `pos` = index of the `{{`.
- Tag (other than a comment) with an empty name: `pos` = start of the tag.
- Closing without an open section, or with a name different from the innermost open section: `pos` = start of the closing tag.
- Section not closed at the end of the template: `pos` = start of the opening tag of the **innermost** open section.

## Examples

- `render('{{#xs}}{{@index}}:{{.}};{{/xs}}', { xs: ['a', 'b'] })` → `'0:a;1:b;'`
- `render('{{#user}}{{name}} @{{site}}{{/user}}', { site: 'X', user: { name: 'Ana' } })` → `'Ana @X'`
- `render('Itens:\n{{#xs}}\n- {{.}}\n{{/xs}}\nfim', { xs: ['a', 'b'] })` → `'Itens:\n- a\n- b\nfim'`
- `render('{{#item}}[{{nota}}]{{/item}}', { nota: 'global', item: { nota: undefined } })` → `'[]'`
- `parse('{{#a}}{{#b}}{{/a}}{{/b}}')` → `TemplateError` with `pos === 12`.

bugs.summary: lookup stops at the first context whose value is not null/undefined (ctx[head] != null) instead of the first one that has the property (head in ctx)
